name: Insomniac
description: The commander barely sleeps; the night is there to be used, at a price.
upside: Night slot always available (not only on events).
downside: -1 effective Empathy rank on the day after a sleepless night.

name: Old Wound
description: The commander has been hurt before and it shows; the squad respects that, and so does the next fight.
upside: Seasoning +1 at start; Trust gains +15% for the first 14 days ("seen worse").

name: Silver Tongue
description: Words come easily to the commander, and so do half-truths.
downside: Units with the trigger "lies" punish a detected lie harder.

name: Pretty Face
description: People notice the commander first and judge second.
downside: Trust gains -10% for the first 14 days ("corporate doll").

name: Bookish
description: The commander learns from files and people before learning from drills.

name: Field Medic
description: The commander was trained to patch people up, and they remember who did.
upside: Medbay actions with a unit give +Affinity; Empathy starts at rank 2.

name: Corporate Polish
description: The commander speaks the corporation's language fluently, which opens doors and closes hearts.
upside: +1 Leash authorization per week; oversight standing +.
downside: Units whose values lean against the corporation start with Trust -10.

name: Street-Raised
description: The commander grew up below the corporate floors and knows how things really get done.
upside: Cunning starts at rank 2; requisition prices -15%.
downside: Corporate standing -; the Leash is approved less often.

name: Vow of Distance
description: AUTHOR TO WRITE: a vow that keeps the commander from anything romantic and makes a deeper kind of closeness possible.
upside: Platonic closeness comes 15% easier; a unique platonic bond (sworn) becomes possible.

name: Secret Frequency
description: AUTHOR TO WRITE: an experimental frequency analyzer in the commander's head picks up fragments of the squad's thoughts. If the squad finds out, it ends badly.
upside: Fragments of what a soldier hides reach the commander in scenes and messages.
downside: Some fragments are false, and acting on one gives the commander away. Discovery crashes Trust.
changes: Scenes and messages sometimes bring a fragment of what a soldier hides: her stance, a demand, a warning, a secret.
A fragment is never marked true or false. Some are distorted, some name only the subject.
Acting on what the commander could not know makes a soldier suspicious. Some soldiers sense it sooner.
A soldier who is sure has leverage over the commander, and the squad finds out. Trust and Affinity crash.
The implant can be burned out in the medbay. That is permanent, and it softens a later discovery.

name: Bloom-induced Paranoia
description: AUTHOR TO WRITE: long exposure to the Bloom left the commander's mind not quite right. Something is always about to go wrong.
upside: Loyalty warnings arrive one or two days early as PREMONITIONs. A new order, Contingency, covers the commander against a soldier who turns.
downside: Some premonitions are false and look exactly like real ones. Nightmares raise stress and can cost a morning.
changes: Warning signs of doubt, desertion, mutiny and defiance reach the commander early as PREMONITIONs.
Each day a soldier may also trigger a false alarm, and nothing in the notice tells it apart.
Acting on a real warning can head it off. Acting on a false one is an insult or a coercion with full consequences.
Bloom nightmares add commander stress, can cost the next morning, and sometimes bring a soldier to the door.
At high stress the commander reads people worse. Sleep and the medbay bring it down.

name: Web of Debts
description: AUTHOR TO WRITE: old mistakes and shady ties. The commander must feed information to a rival corporation.
upside: A handler from a rival corporation pays supplies, credits and plyx for intel.
downside: What is sold comes back as ambushes, sabotage and shifts in standing. Oversight and the squad can find out.
changes: About once a week a handler visits at night and buys intel on missions, the base and the squad.
For each item the commander answers: truth, partial, false or withhold.
Truthful intel comes back as ambushes on expeditions, sabotage at the base and changes in standing.
Withholding raises the handler's pressure, and a handler pushed far enough leaks the commander's crime to the squad.
Oversight and watchful soldiers can find out. Each ending is a choice with a cost.
